chunks: Then those striking sparks of fire,

key_terms.الْمُورِيَاتِ: Those that strike sparks (referring to horses)

ai.seo_question: What does 'Al-Muriyat Qadhan' mean in the Quran?
ai.summary: This fragment from the opening of Surah Al-Adiyat vividly depicts warhorses striking fire from their hooves, a imagery Shia exegetes often link to the martial prowess of the early Muslim cavalry and the spiritual readiness of the Imams. The term 'Al-Muriyat' (those that draw out) emphasizes the deliberate, forceful action of the steeds, symbolizing the active struggle (Jihad) and the extraction of victory through divine support. This verse sets the tone for the subsequent rhetorical questions challenging those who deny the Resurrection, contrasting the tangible power of the charger with the unseen reality of the Hereafter.
